info.title: SecurityScorecard API
info.description:
REST API for the SecurityScorecard platform: manage portfolios, companies, scores, findings, and integrations.

This documentation is built from two kinds of sources.

## Internal API docs (`servicesWithInternalApiDocs`)

Specs are fetched at runtime from other microservices/repositories. Those sections are dynamic and reflect the live specs exposed by each service.

- [audit](https://users.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [authentication-policies](https://users.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [eval](https://eval.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [feedback](https://measurements.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [fluxus](https://fluxus-rest-api.prod.ssc.camp/docs/fluxus.json)
- [footprint](https://footprint.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [managed-services](https://users.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [max](https://max-api.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [measurements](https://measurements.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [plans](https://plans.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [subscriptions](https://subscriptions.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [users](https://users.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)
- [zzzzzz](https://users.prod.ssc.camp/api-docs)

## External API docs (`servicesWithExternalApiDocs`)

Specs are bundled in this repository (local Swagger 2.0 files or static definitions). They are versioned and maintained here rather than fetched from elsewhere.

Token.name: Authorization
Token.description:
SecurityScorecard API endpoints require an authentication token to be passed
in an authorization header in order to return data. If you do not already
have a token, you can create one by going to the API Access area in your
[Settings page](https://platform.securityscorecard.io/#/settings/api) and then
clicking Generate New Token. Please note this tokens have no expiration
so they can be used until manually revoked. If you have a token and generate
a new one, the previous token will be revoked and can no longer be used.

Administrators can also revoke API tokens for any user in their account.

Once you have your token you can pass it in using the `Authorization` http header like this:

```
curl -X GET \
  https://api.securityscorecard.io/portfolios \
  -H 'authorization: Token <your token>'
```

event_type.description:
the type of event, at the moment one of these:
- `issues`: indicates the arrival or departure of issues to this scorecard
- `breach`: a breach was associated to this company
- `recalibration`: indicates a recalibration event

Note: additional event types might be introduced in the future.

group_status.description:
when event type is "issues" indicates
the status of the associated group of issues, at the moment one of:
- `active`: new issues have been observed
- `resolved`: issues were refuted and resolution confirmed by SecurityScorecard
- `departed`: issues are not observed anymore

issue_count.description:
when event type is "issues" indicates
the number of issue findings associated to this event

total_score_impact.description:
total score impact of the findings detected in the event, to
the company's overall score

issue_type.description:
when event type is "issues" indicates
the type of the associated issues, one of the
[existing issue types](#tag/metadata%2Fpaths%2F~1metadata~1issue-types%2Fget)

breach_data.description:
when event type is "breach" includes
additional information about the breach.

Important Note: the fields available here might change in the future.

breach_incidents.description:
when issue type is "confirmed_first_party_breach",
"confirmed_third_party_breach", "alleged_first_party_breach", or
"alleged_third_party_breach", lists the individual breach incidents
from the breach-ages API for this effective date. Each entry represents
a distinct breach incident that may share the same scoring date. Only
present when incident data is available.

factor.description: factor the associated issue type belongs to

detail_url.description: api endpoint to get the issue findings detail of this event
